However, the camera-to-LiDAR projection throws away the semantic density of camera features, hindering the effectiveness of such methods, especially for semantic-oriented tasks (such as 3D scene segmentation).
To achieve this, we diagnose and lift the key efficiency bottlenecks in the view transformation with optimized BEV pooling, reducing latency by more than 40×.

solution.summary: In this paper, we propose BEVFusion, an efficient and generic multi-task multi-sensor fusion framework. In this paper, we propose BEVFusion to unify multi-modal features in a shared bird’s-eye view (BEV) representation space for task-agnostic learning.

In this paper, we propose BEVFusion to unify multi-modal features in a shared bird’s-eye view (BEV) representation space for task-agnostic learning.

limitations.summary: On the one hand, the LiDARto-BEV projection flattens the sparse LiDAR features along the height dimension, thus does not create geometric distortion in Figure 1a.
items: On the one hand, the LiDARto-BEV projection flattens the sparse LiDAR features along the height dimension, thus does not create geometric distortion in Figure 1a.

This kernel removes the dependency between outputs (thus does not require multi-level tree reduction) and avoids writing the partial sums to the DRAM, reducing the latency of feature aggregation from 500ms to 2ms (Figure 3c).
In contrast, our techniques are exact without any approximation, while still being faster.
Our method could potentially benefit from more accurate depth estimation (e.g., supervising the view transformer with groundtruth depth [42], [53]), which we leave for future work.
